claim_scope: high average transition agreement can coexist with a decision-critical model error
a planner can exploit one optimistic model error and reverse the true policy ranking
world-model utility must be measured with downstream return gaps and held-out true-environment anchors
an explicit observed-support gate rejects the unsupported shortcut in this fixture and changes the selected policy
the same gate accepts the erroneous shortcut and preserves exploitation regret when that state-action is authored as covered
distinct transition, state-decoder, and outcome-scorer faults can be observationally equivalent at the final proxy-score interface
perfect retrospective ranking on a frozen two-policy panel does not guarantee ranking of a disjoint policy introduced after calibration
two models with the same uniform transition accuracy can have different policy-selection regret when their sole error occurs at a candidate-reachable versus currently unvisited query

code.config: standard-library v6 corridor transition, equal-accuracy fault allocation, policy-ranking, prospective split, support-gate, and four-component attribution fixture

limitations: hand-authored deterministic corridor rather than a learned neural world model
three fixed policies and one deliberately optimistic shortcut error
return units and effect sizes do not represent any real task
no images, learned uncertainty estimator, policy training, simulator, robot, vehicle, or GPU
both support declarations are hand-authored rather than learned coverage estimates
support membership cannot detect errors inside observed support or shared model bias
component scenarios inject one deterministic fault at a time and do not estimate prevalence, interactions, independence, or an additive error budget
the state decoder is represented by a terminal-label interface rather than learned pose, depth, or event extraction
the prospective panel contains only one authored held-out policy and does not estimate generalization across learned policy families, checkpoints, tasks, or initial-state shifts
a two-policy Spearman value is a fragile ordering check rather than a calibrated correlation estimate
the unvisited wait fault is unvisited only by this fixed candidate panel and can become decision-critical under another policy, initial state, or planner
